subject: Request: hard model tether for PulseHealth pilot (US-only, enforcement)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: hard model tether for PulseHealth pilot (US-only, enforcement)

Team —

PulseHealth (platform security lead copied below) has finalized their pilot SOW and it's gated on two infra constraints we need to evaluate:

1) Model tether: they require all traffic from their tenant to be served by a single vetted variant (redwood-q4-7b-priv-enc) with enforced routing — no automatic fallback to other model families for the duration of the pilot.
2) US residency: traffic must stay in us-west regions; no cross-region routing allowed.

Why? Their compliance certification requires a deterministic model binary in the execution path for audit reproducibility. They view automatic fallbacks as an unacceptable source of drift.

Ask: can Product + Infra provision a routing policy that: (a) pins requests for PulseHealth to the variant above, (b) blocks fallback behavior for that tenant (raising errors instead of routing to an alternate), and (c) enforces region == us-west? They want this live by Nov 9 for the security review.

Traffic profile: expected 200–400 requests/minute during weekday peak, mostly short chats (avg 120 tokens). We expect some burst capacity during demo runs.

I attached the SOW excerpt and a draft routing-exception form. Initial approvals needed: Product (policy + UX), Infra (capacity + kernel support for the quantized variant), Security (audit logging/KMS posture). Legal will also sign the exception because it changes standard SLA/fallback behavior.

Notes: this is not a permanent requirement — pilot window is Nov 9–Dec 31 — but the request is strict for that window.

Next steps: Karthik, can you confirm infra constraints and whether autoscale + reservation is sufficient? Lauren, would you own the exception request to the Routing Exceptions board if infra gives a green light?

Thanks,
—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: PulseHealth_MATP_SOW.xlsx (excel)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: hard model tether for PulseHealth pilot (US-only, enforcement)

Marissa —

Short answer: technically feasible, long answer: we need to flag a few operational trade-offs so leadership understands the risk/impact. Quick points:

- Routing: we can add a tenant-scoped policy that maps PulseHealth to redwood-q4-7b-priv-enc and mark it non-fallbackable. That will cause requests to fail with a 503-style error when the variant is unavailable (instead of failing over).
- Capacity: to avoid failure windows we'll need reserved capacity or hard capacity reservations on the dedicated pool (or soft overprovisioning in hosted), depending on whether this runs on Dedicated or Hosted. For the traffic you quoted, a small reserved pool (1–2 GPUs depending on model perf) should be adequate.
- Monitoring: we must wire token-level traces and a synthetic probe to detect silent perf regressions; otherwise customer will see unexplained errors.
- KMS/audit: if they require a self-managed KMS or HSM, we need Security to confirm key access patterns; otherwise we can use our managed KMS but must document access logs.

Questions:
1) Is PulseHealth asking that we block any programmatic fallback including regional fallback and model-family fallback? Or just family fallback?
2) Which deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated) do they expect? Dedicated makes reservations straightforward; hosted needs a capacity commit.

If you want, I can draft the infra section for the routing-exception form and a quick capacity estimate for the commit.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Serving Infrastructure

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: hard model tether for PulseHealth pilot (US-only, enforcement)

Thanks — I reviewed the SOW and Karthik's notes. Principle: we're open to one-off enforced tethers for pilots when there's a clear compliance need, but we must gate them through the Routing Exceptions board and Security sign-off. Operational asks:

- Marissa: please complete the routing-exception-form.pdf (attached) with the exact failure semantics you want (error code, retry-window) and confirm whether the tenant prefers outage vs degraded response.
- Karthik: please include a capacity & availability runbook and a rollback plan if the reserved pool experiences a hardware fault.
- Security: need confirmation of acceptable KMS setups; if PulseHealth insists on customer-managed keys, Legal will have to scope changes to the agreement.

I'll own the board submission once attachments are filled. Assuming infra confirms reservation and Security signs off, we can accept the exception for the stated pilot window. If anything changes (duration/variant), we re-evaluate.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
VP, Product Management
[Attachment: routing-exception-form.pdf]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: PulseHealth Ops <ops@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: PulseHealth Legal <legal@pulsehealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: hard model tether for PulseHealth pilot (US-only, enforcement)

Hi team —

Looping you in on our internal path forward. TL;DR: Redwood can support a tenant-scoped enforced tether to redwood-q4-7b-priv-enc in us-west only, but we need PulseHealth to: (1) confirm the exact failure semantics (prefer explicit errors over silent fallback), (2) sign the routing exception addendum so Legal can update SLAs, and (3) confirm KMS preference.

Next actions for PulseHealth:
- Please review the SOW excerpt I attached and confirm which of the two failure behaviors you prefer (hard error vs. soft degrade).
- If you require customer-managed keys, let us know contact and KMS details so Security can scope integration.
- Sign and return the routing-exception-form.pdf so we can submit to the Routing Exceptions board.

Target: internal approval and infra reservation by Nov 5 so we can be live Nov 9 for the security review.

Thanks — happy to sync on a quick call if helpful.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: PulseHealth_MATP_SOW.xlsx, routing-exception-form.pdf]
